optcompR

Unified mathematical optimization and computational modeling in R.

optcompR is a solver independent modeling layer. Variables, parameters, constraints and objectives are written with ordinary R operators; models are classified (LP, MILP, QP, MIQP, QCQP, MIQCQP, SOCP, CONIC, NLP, MINLP) with recorded convexity evidence, lowered to sparse standard forms and solved by installed backends. Results carry standardized statuses, duals with one documented sign convention, and diagnostics recomputed independently from the model.

library(optcompR)

m <- opt_model("max")
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", lower = 0)
y <- opt_variable(m, "y", lower = 0)
cap <- opt_constraint(m, x + y <= 4, name = "capacity")
opt_constraint(m, x <= 2)
opt_constraint(m, y <= 3)
opt_objective(m, 3 * x + 2 * y)

r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_status(r)          # "optimal"
opt_value(r, c(x, y))  # 2 2
opt_dual(r, cap)       # shadow price 2
opt_check(r)           # independent feasibility and KKT checks

Features

  • Vectorized expressions with sparse Matrix support, built in milliseconds for 1e5 terms.
  • Parameters for reusable models, scenario sweeps and warm starts.
  • Exact gradients, Jacobians and Lagrangian Hessians of every model function.
  • External R functions with supplied, jaxR or explicitly labeled finite difference gradients.
  • Sensitivity: duals as derivatives of the optimal value, HiGHS ranging, fixed relaxations of MILPs.
  • Multiobjective scalarizations: weighted sums, lexicographic order and epsilon constraints.
  • Exact feasibility and optimality certificates for LP and MILP through Z3 (z3r).
  • Second-order, semidefinite, exponential and power cone constraints.
  • Indicator constraints, SOS1 and SOS2 sets, complementarity and logical constraints, native in SCIP and exactly reformulated elsewhere.
  • Mixed-integer nonlinear programming by NLP branch and bound.
  • Robust constraints (box, budget, ellipsoid), Gaussian and scenario chance constraints, CVaR, sample average and distributionally robust expectations.
  • Derivatives of optimal solutions with respect to parameters by implicit differentiation of the KKT conditions.
  • Least squares fitting of modelcompR ODE models with exact sensitivities.
  • Conversion to and from symcompR expressions.

Solver support

Backend Package Classes Global for Duals Ranging Warm start
highs highs LP, MILP, convex QP all of these LP, QP LP yes
clarabel clarabel LP, convex QP, SOCP, CONIC (SOC, PSD, exp, power) all of these yes no no
scip scip LP, MILP, QP, MIQP, QCQP, MIQCQP, SOCP, MISOCP all, including nonconvex no no no
osqp osqp convex QP, LP convex problems yes no no
nloptr nloptr NLP, QCQP, QP, LP (SLSQP) convex problems estimated no start point
ipopt IPOPT library NLP, QCQP, QP, LP (exact Hessians) convex problems yes no start point
nlpbb nloptr MINLP, MIQCQP, MIQP convex relaxations no no no
roi ROI + plugin plugin classes plugin plugin no no

HiGHS is required; the others are optional. The IPOPT backend is compiled in when pkg-config finds IPOPT at installation (brew install ipopt, apt install coinor-libipopt-dev); check with opt_ipopt_available().

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/optcompR")

Optional integrations: remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/z3r") (needs the Z3 library), remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/symcompR"), remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/jaxR"), remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/modelcompR").

Documentation

Articles at https://adamrsophie.github.io/optcompR/ cover linear, quadratic, mixed-integer, nonlinear, conic, robust, stochastic and multiobjective optimization, indicator and SOS constraints, parameterized and sparse models, solver comparison, diagnostics, infeasible models, sensitivity, derivatives of optimal solutions, exact certificates, ODE fitting and the underlying concepts.
